decision_table.name: Determine_KY_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Kentucky state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in KY (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
KY filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in KY if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in KY - Employees working in KY - Tangible personal property located in KY - Real property located in KY
Reference: KRS 141.010 (Nexus definitions) Reference: KRS 141.120 (Apportionment and nexus requirements) Reference: Kentucky Form 720 Instructions (Filing requirements)

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
KY filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts OR 200 transactions in KY.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), KY requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus thresholds, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: KRS 139.340 (Economic nexus for sales tax - applies by analogy) Reference: Kentucky Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance

No KY nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: KRS 141.120 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_KY_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate KY state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
KY state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
KY ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to KY) - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction addback (KY decouples) - State income tax refunds that were deducted federally - Bonus depreciation adjustments (KY may require conformity modifications) - Expenses related to tax-exempt income
KY SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on KY state and municipal bonds - Dividends from Kentucky corporations (100% deduction for qualifying dividends) - Kentucky net operating loss deduction (subject to KY limitations) - Certain dividend income eligible for KY dividend received deduction
Reference: Kentucky Form 720 Schedule A (Additions to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Kentucky Form 720 Schedule M (Subtractions from Federal Taxable Income) Reference: KRS 141.010 (Definitions of Kentucky taxable income) Reference: KRS 141.039 (Adjustments to federal taxable income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have KY nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_KY_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate KY state corporate income tax. Applies KY 4.5% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
KY state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to KY: × [KY apportionment percentage] 3. KY additions: + [Federal interest, IRC 199A addback, etc.] 4. KY subtractions: - [KY municipal interest, KY dividends, KY NOL, etc.] 5. KY taxable income: = [Result] 6. KY tax rate: × 4.5% (flat rate, effective 2025) 7. KY income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. KY credits: - [Industrial development, film, coal, recycling, R&D, etc.] 9. KY tax liability: = [Final tax]
KY uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
KY tax rate history: - 2025+: 4.5% (flat rate) - 2019-2024: 5% (flat rate) - Before 2019: Progressive rates with brackets
KY provides various tax credits including: - Industrial Development Tax Credits (KRS 141.347) - Film Industry Tax Credit (KRS 148.542) - Coal Incentive Tax Credit (KRS 141.428) - Recycling and Composting Equipment Tax Credit (KRS 141.390) - Research and Development Tax Credit (KRS 141.396) - Angel Investor Tax Credit (KRS 141.396)
Note: KY also imposes Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET) on gross receipts, which is calculated separately and not included in this table.
Reference: Kentucky Form 720 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: KRS 141.040 (Tax rate of 4.5%) Reference: KRS 141.120 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: Kentucky Department of Revenue Corporation Tax Instructions

No KY nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in KY. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: KRS 141.120 (Nexus requirements)

No KY taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has KY nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
KY net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - KY allows NOL carryforward for 20 years (KRS 141.010(10)(i)) - No carryback allowed (as of 2025) - NOL deduction limited by KY law
Note: Even with no income tax liability, corporations may still owe Kentucky Limited Liability Entity Tax (LLET) based on gross receipts.
Reference: Kentucky Form 720 (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: KRS 141.010(10)(i) (Net operating loss provisions)
